name: Waldorf Astoria Los Cabos Pedregal
positioning: Secluded cliffside resort carved into the mountain at the tip of the Baja California Peninsula, reached through a private tunnel, where every room has its own plunge pool and Pacific views
best_for: Couples who want privacy, a plunge pool and ocean views from their own room
Food and spirits lovers drawn to seafood, champagne and agave tastings
Spa-goers interested in treatments rooted in Mexican folk healing

facts.text: The resort sits where the Pacific Ocean meets the Sea of Cortez, on the southern tip of Mexico's Baja California Peninsula.
The resort covers 24 acres and is carved into the mountain.
Stays come with bespoke service from the resort's butlers and Personal Concierge team.
Guests are welcomed in their room with a bottle of premium tequila as a gift.
Don Manuel's serves casual breakfast and lunch, then turns into fine dining in the evening with live local musicians.
El Farallon's Champagne Terrace offers a curated collection of 20 rotating champagnes.
Mar y Lena is the resort's signature steakhouse, with wood-fired cooking at The Beach Club Palapa.
The spa's wet-area grottos have steam rooms, saunas, ice rooms and whirlpools.
The Intention spa treatment was developed with local curanderos and shamans and includes an energy cleansing ritual, craniosacral therapy and a Mexican folk massage.
Complimentary yoga classes are offered, and there are two tennis courts with a tennis pro.
From December to April, small-group whale watching trips follow the whales' annual migration.
Excursions include Panga reef cruises, surfing lessons, breakfast on the resort's private yacht and farm-to-table lunches in Todos Santos.

highlights.text: Guests enter the resort through the private Dos Mares tunnel.
Every accommodation has its own private plunge pool and Pacific Ocean views.
At El Farallon, overlooking the Pacific, the local fishermen's catch is prepared in an open-air kitchen.
A saltwater meditation pool is reached directly from the spa's private treatment rooms.
The Agave Study at Peacock Alley offers tastings of agave spirits, from tequila in Jalisco to mezcal in Oaxaca.

considerations.text: Conde Nast Traveler notes that because the resort faces the Pacific, strong waves and a constant undercurrent mean ocean swimming is prohibited.
The resort sits in a secluded enclave behind a private mountain tunnel, with very little within walking distance.
Because of the cliffside location and multi-level design, travelers with limited mobility may encounter challenges.
